root_cause.text: `make_task_dead()` in `kernel/exit.c` called `do_task_dead()` with preemption still enabled after setting an oopsing task to `EXIT_DEAD/TASK_DEAD`, allowing the dead task to be preempted before `__schedule()`, which breaks scheduler assumptions and can lead to stack use-after-free/double-free.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `preempt_disable();` immediately before `do_task_dead();`, and the CVE text says this path was previously “with preemption enabled,” which is “forbidden” because `do_task_dead()` calls `__schedule()` and a preempted `TASK_DEAD` task causes `finish_task_switch()` to repeatedly drop references on the dead task’s stack.
